samples.summary: New regression guard hard-codes 5xx → exit 1 / code "ERROR", contradicting the documented error matrix (5xx → exit 2 / SYSTEM), so it will block the spec-conforming fix
samples.evidence: The new end-to-end guard asserts `body.error` equals `{ code: 'ERROR', message: 'HTTP 500' }` and `process.exitCode === 1` for a stubbed HTTP 500 (packages/cli/test/output.test.ts:269-277). The spec this PR is aligning `--quiet` to states the opposite for that case: docs/design/cli.md:952 `| Backend 5xx or network | 2 | SYSTEM | (original message preserved) |` (and :951 for 401/403 → 2/UNAUTHORIZED). The production path that produces the asserted values is docs.ts:117 `throw new Error(\`HTTP ${res.status}\`)` → formatter.ts:52-57 which always emits code `ERROR` and exitCode 1. Nothing else in the tree asserts the 5xx envelope, so this test becomes the de-facto contract and any later change to honour the documented exit-2/SYSTEM mapping now fails a test whose subject is `--quiet`, not exit codes. Fix belongs on the new test: assert only that stderr got a non-empty envelope and that the exit code is non-zero.

samples.summary: New tests drive commander without `exitOverride()`; any parse error calls `process.exit()` and kills the whole packages/cli vitest worker instead of failing one test
samples.evidence: `run()` calls `buildProgram().parseAsync([...])` (packages/cli/test/output.test.ts:239-241) on a program built by `createProgram()` (packages/cli/src/commands/root.ts:42-63), which never calls `.exitOverride()` or `.configureOutput()`. This is the first test in the package that actually parses argv — every other cli test invokes the pure `run*` orchestrators directly (e.g. packages/cli/test/docs-content.test.ts, notes-import.test.ts). Commander's error paths (unknown option, missing required argument, `--help`/`--version`) end in `process.exit()`, which in a vitest worker aborts the entire file/worker, so a future rename of `docs list` / `sheets cells get` or of a global flag turns into an opaque "worker terminated" failure across the whole cli suite rather than a single red test. Adding `program.exitOverride()` (and asserting on the thrown CommanderError) in `buildProgram()` contains the blast radius.
